last_updated: After DeepSeek provider migration (Decision 017); OpenAI Responses API integration verification remains accurate as an M1-era historical record below

major_debugging_history.solution: Migrated provider implementation to OpenAI Responses API
Added layered logging in Route, Planning Engine and OpenAI Adapter

major_debugging_history.problem: Node fetch timed out while browser access worked
major_debugging_history.solution: Identified that the development terminal was not using the proxy

major_debugging_history.problem: curl worked but Node fetch still timed out
major_debugging_history.solution: Configured HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY / ALL_PROXY for the development environment
Unified fetch and ProxyAgent to use the same undici implementation instead of mixing Node built-in fetch with npm undici

current_provider.status: Switched via Decision 017; pending live re-verification with a real DEEPSEEK_API_KEY

engineering_notes: Provider abstraction successfully minimized migration cost from Anthropic to OpenAI, and again from OpenAI to DeepSeek.
End-to-end validation was completed before expanding product functionality.
Node.js networking differs from browser networking and requires independent validation.
Proxy configuration should always be verified separately from application logic.

The OpenAI Responses API was validated as a working provider interface at M1, but was not the long-term provider — DeepSeek is now the default (Decision 017). Provider swaps should be expected to recur; the composition root is what makes them cheap, not any one provider's permanence.
known_limitations: Current planning generation still uses the temporary smoke-test prompt.
Production-quality planning prompt has not yet been implemented.
DEEPSEEK_API_KEY in .env.local is currently a placeholder (empty) — live success-path and error-path verification against the real DeepSeek API is still pending.
next_objectives: Replace the smoke-test prompt with the production planning prompt
important_context: Do not redesign the Provider abstraction.
Focus Phase 2 on product capability rather than infrastructure.
Treat the project documentation as the source of truth.
